As trispecifics, cell engagers and other complex formats multiply, drug developers are seeking discovery and engineering partners to help navigate an expanding universe of molecular possibilities.
For every new binding arm added to a molecule construct, the number of potential combinations expands, making molecule selection an increasingly complex exercise. As multispecific formats proliferate, service providers are increasingly working with sponsors to determine which molecule to build in the first place.
Challenges present in determining which format, affinity profile and molecular architecture are most likely to balance efficacy, safety, manufacturability and developability. As a result, the infrastructure of discovery and engineering partners is growing beyond simple antibody generation to support shared strategic decision-making in molecular design.
As BioSpace previously reported , bispecifics established the first generation of multitarget biologics. Bispecifics are immunotherapies designed with two different “arms” that can bind to two separate targets simultaneously. They have made trade news headlines as Chinese biotechs launched an unprecedented wave of bispecific programs between 2020 and 2025.
The next wave of multispecifics include trispecifics, T-cell engagers with co‑stimulation, NK engagers and dual agonists. Their development poses new considerations beyond bispecifics’ inherent complexity.
Varied multispecific options
As the number of possible molecules grows, the greater goal has shifted from candidate discovery to selection.
The benefit of multispecifics is they allow greater possibilities to fight cancer, said Roland Green, CEO, co-founder and chairman of antibody discovery, design and delivery company Invenra. In the case of trispecific antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), the addition of a third arm can be used to drive better internalization of ADC payloads. In laymen’s terms, this means the tumor can absorb the drug more effectively.
In terms of the trispecific landscape, T cell engagers are quite common, where one arm binds the T cell from the immune system and the others bind to tumor cells. Pharma clients are also very interested in cell engagers, Green said, where one arm binds to an immune cell, one arm to the tumor and a third arm that binds to the first immune cell. The final arm acts as co-stimulant and boosts the potential for the body’s immune cells to attack the tumor.
“You don’t build a more complex molecule just because you can,” Green noted. “You build a molecule to solve a problem that hasn’t been solved.”
Molecule format decision-making
Screening methodologies need to match that complexity with the relevant throughput, said Oren Beske, head of biologics at Twist Bioscience. In February, Twist announced that it had entered into a licensing agreement to become the co-exclusive provider, together with Invenra, of the latter’s’ B-Body® bispecific antibody platform.
Often, the nuances and biological relevance of matching the desired affinities to multiple targets within a single molecule makes this task formidable, Beske said. There can be hundreds of combinations to be considered for bispecifics and potentially thousands for trispecifics.
Usually, a partner hopes a multispecific molecule, when binding to specified targets and in a particular format, will address their chosen disease biology, said Eric Krauland. Krauland is president and chief science officer at Adimab, which offers an antibody discovery and engineering platform.
If the partner does not have a format they want to work with, Adimab will typically guide partners toward IgG-like/full Fab-based multispecifics rather than using scFv-based multispecifics to facilitate manufacturing, he added.
Fab fragments are the first two domains of both an antibody heavy chain (HC) and light chain (LC), with the first domain of each chain containing the regions that confer target specificity. An scFv (single-chain variable fragment) is just those two binding domains, one from each chain, linked together in a single protein by inserting a flexible peptide sequence.
Adimab is seeing more projects featuring unvalidated biology and sponsors that are keen to explore multiple format configurations. T cell engagers have driven significant interest following clinical validation; sponsor goals are now shifting to increase potency and safety. When it comes to T cell engagers, the company offers a panel of CD3 antibodies that have a wide range of affinities.
Controlling heterogeneity
Solutions aim to reduce the amount of heavy chain/heavy chain (HC/HC) and heavy chain/light chain (HC/LC) mispairing and increase usable product for later downstream manufacturing, Krauland said.
Mispairing can cause heterogeneity, but heterogeneity has multiple causes besides mispairing. For the latter, the final product becomes an undesirable blend of multiple molecular species rather than one uniform molecule.
Eleva Biologics’ two moss-specific platform capabilities significantly reduce heterogeneity from the outset, said Björn Cochlovius, CEO and managing director. They allow correct folding and multimeric assembly, handled natively by plant-specific chaperones. This is a space where other approaches often struggle, he said.
“By avoiding product heterogeneity and reducing analytical and QC complexity, the platform can help shortens timelines, lowers cost of goods and delivers cleaner chemistry, manufacturing and controls,” he said.
Concentrated engineering exercise
An important quality to consider at the molecular creation stage is developability, which includes expressability, Krauland said. Developability considers how suitable a molecule is for successful drug development beyond its biological activity. Expressability is how easily and efficiently a cell can produce the molecule. Aggregation is also a key factor to consider and can be attributed both to the antibody components and to the multispecific format chosen. It’s an important consideration because aggregation can negatively affect the yield at the end of the purification as well as portend downstream issues, such as shelf-life stability and immunogenicity.
Other general properties that can signal developability challenges, are hydrophobicity—a molecule’s tendency to repel water—and polyreactivity, or “stickiness”, a molecule’s tendency to weakly interact with many other substrates. Hydrophobicity can influence a molecule’s stability, and overall ease of downstream manufacturing. Stickiness can lead to formulation challenges, as well as possible pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic issues once the therapeutic is administered into the body.
From promise to proof
The challenge of addressing these molecular properties is one reason why next-generation formats such as trispecifics have been slower to mature than their bispecific predecessors.
Trispecifics are at the stage where bispecifics were five years ago, Green said. Their complexity in terms of design and manufacturing has meant the industry is nascent, so there needs to be some success stories before there is large-scale investment.
“The bigger question to ask on developing increasingly complicated molecules beyond the multispecifics of today (such as cytokine fusions, radiotherapies and ADCs) is whether doing so will benefit patients beyond the current tried and true modalities,” Beske said. “Of course, time and appropriate investments will be required to answer that question.”

Sample Collection Mission to Martian Moons Gets Going This Week, Phobos and Deimos in the Crosshairs
13 photos
Photo: JAXA
Since the Mariner 4 mission performed the first successful flyby of planet Mars in the 1960s, there have been some 50 different missions to the Red Planet. About half of them ended in success, but none have brought back samples of the planet’s surface or pieces of its moons. But that’s about to change soon.
After years upon years of research and development, the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is expected to leave Earth this week. Run by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) with assistance from NASA and a number of private contractors, the mission’s main goal is to expand our understanding of the two Martian moons, in the hopes that they could also expand our understanding of the solar system and our own planet.
Mars has two moons, named Phobos and Deimos. We have known of their existence since 1877, when they were first discovered by American astronomer Asaph Hall. They are much smaller than our own (Phobos is the larger of the two), and somewhat weirdly shaped.
At the moment, our species doesn’t really know how they came to be: they either formed from Martian ejecta resulting from an asteroid impact, kind of like we think our Moon formed, or they are asteroids themselves, captured by Mars’ gravity before they could crash or escape.
There are a number of things we do know about the two moons. Phobos, for instance, makes a complete circle around Mars three times per day, moving closer and closer to the surface, at a rate of some six feet (1.8 meters) every hundred years.
Photo: JAXA Some 50 million years from now, this behavior will probably end with it crashing into Mars or breaking up in a sort of orbital ring of debris. The smaller Moon, Deimos, is a bit calmer, spinning around the Red Planet every 30 hours, in what appears to be a stable orbit.
The MMX spacecraft that will be sent to have a closer look at the two is a chemically powered machine comprised of three main modules: the exploration module, the propulsion module, and the return module.
The ship's main body is where the lander, systems, and subsystems are housed, and solar panels are on deck to power all of that. Rounding off the manifest are a high-gain dish antenna to ensure communications, a camera, and LiDAR.
Three main instruments are on board, namely the two coring and pneumatic samplers (C- and P-sampler), and a spectrograph called MEGANE, each with its own role to play in the mission. The samplers are, of course, the most important of them all.
Photo: JAXA JAXA will use MMX to descend to the surface of the moon Phobos, and use the C- and P-sampler installed on one of its landing legs to collect a ground sample. Each of the two designs is meant to work in a different way.
The C-sampler, for instance, is to dig into the moon’s surface a few inches and collect samples from there. The P, on the other hand, will do so by using bursts of high-pressure nitrogen gas meant to send material flying freely, ready to be captured.
It’s unclear how much Phobos material the mission is expected to collect, but all of it will be brought back to our planet inside sample canisters, and it will be used to learn more about how the Martian moons came to be.
I mentioned earlier the MEGANE instrument. Taking after the Japanese word that stands for eyeglasses and at the same time an acronym for Mars-moon Exploration with GAmma rays and Neutrons, the tool is a spectrograph meant to measure the neutrons and gamma rays emitted from the moon’s surface in a bid to determine what it’s made of, chemically speaking.
Photo: JAXA The Japanese space agency plans to launch the MMX mission on October 19, using an H3 rocket taking off from the Tanegashima Space Center in Japan. If, for some reason, that doesn't happen, the launch window stays open until November 8.
The spacecraft is expected to reach its destination in August 2027 and spend more than a year studying the planet’s moons. The actual sample collection is expected to take place in December 2028, with the Phobos material set to be brought back to Earth in 2031.
Whatever quantity of material will reach our world will be shared with scientists around the world, with some 15 percent of it to go to NASA’s Johnson Space Center Astromaterials Lab in Houston.
Hopes are that a few grams of Martian moon soil would be enough to shed more light on a time when all the inner planets, Earth included, could have acquired most of their water and organic compounds.
We will keep an eye on the MMX mission and report back once we learn that it has launched and is officially on its way to the Red Planet.

source_document.body:
While GLP-1 medicines have become synonymous with weight loss, at least one expert thinks amylin would have been the go-to target if biopharma had been focused on the blockbuster indication 10 years ago. A new wave of therapies is now exploring this potentially gentler mechanism.
As Novo’s amylin/GLP-1 combo CagriSema nears possible FDA approval and amylin-targeting assets from Eli Lilly and Zealand Pharma yield late-stage data, experts are touting the potential of the amylin approach to be a more tolerable option for weight management than the ubiquitously popular GLP-1s.
“It’s a great mechanism that everyone should be paying attention to,” Hyung Heon Kim, president and CEO of MetaVia, said during a BioSpace webinar last month.
BMO Capital Markets Head of Healthcare Research Evan Seigerman agreed, calling amylin “the next hot target” in the obesity space. The weight loss benefits of GLP-1s—initially indicated for diabetes—were a serendipitous discovery, Seigerman noted. But the analyst said he was struck by a comment from a key opinion leader who told him that if the biopharma industry had been focused on weight loss 10 years ago, amylin would have been the target of choice.
Events
Webinar: The Massive Scale of GLP-1s: Evolving Health, Healthcare and Markets
Watch this discussion on how GLP-1 drugs for obesity are changing the shape of U.S. healthcare. From direct-to-consumer portals to pharmacy deals, how these drugs reach patients is changing—and leading to debates over pricing and coverage. Learn how your company can be both patient-forward while also maximizing revenue in this unique environment.

·
1 min read
·

Why amylin?
Eli Lilly’s Zepbound and Novo’s Wegovy, and the other GLP-1 drugs in their portfolios or under development by biopharma writ large, work by activating the GLP-1 receptors to trigger the secretion of insulin and inhibition of glucagon release. In so doing, the medicines help to balance appetite and food cravings.
But they don’t work for everyone, and amylin-targeting molecules could bust through weight loss plateaus in order to treat patients who may not respond well to GLP-1 drugs like Lilly’s Zepbound or Novo’s Wegovy, Seigerman said. “[Key opinion leaders] need something else like this in their armamentarium because not all patients respond to either one of them,” he added.
GLP-1-based medicines also come with myriad side effects, most commonly gastrointestinal. There is a belief among experts that amylin-based weight loss drugs might offer a gentler option, with fewer adverse effects.
Roche CEO Thomas Schinecker talked up the tolerability of his company’s Zealand Pharma–partnered amylin analog petrelintide. “If you don’t want side effects, you can take a highly tolerable amylin” drug, Schinecker told reporters in April during Roche’s first-quarter 2026 earnings call.
Amylin/GLP-1 agonist combo therapies could achieve the same level of weight loss but with better tolerability by including lower doses of GLP-1 than do current monotherapies, Seigerman said. Indeed, Novo in June touted “low” dropout rates in the REDEFINE-1 and REDEFINE-2 trials of CagriSema, which combines semaglutide and the long-acting amylin analog cagrilintide. Patients in REDEFINE-1 lost 22.7% of their body weight at 68 weeks—below Novo’s own projections of around 25% but on par with current GLP-1 drugs.
“Taking the best GLP-1 out there at this point in time, adding essentially an amylin . . . you’re able to get efficacy beyond where people may plateau on [semaglutide] for sure, and maybe even Zepbound,” Seigerman said of CagriSema.
As to the demand for these therapies, Seigerman pointed to the bidding war between Novo and Pfizer last year over fledgling obesity biotech Metsera—a prize Pfizer ultimately won for nearly $10 billion.
“When you talk to Pfizer and Novo about the Metsera bidding war . . . they were both going at this company because they wanted their amylin,” he said. Just months before the bidding war began, an ultra-long-acting amylin injection the biotech was developing elicited 8.4% placebo-adjusted weight loss at 36 days in a Phase 1 trial .
The state of play
Novo is nearing the regulatory finish line with CagriSema. The Danish pharma filed for FDA approval of its amylin combo last December, and analysts are anticipating a decision this quarter.
If approved, CagriSema would be the first amylin drug to hit the market for weight loss, but it has many potential competitors in the pipeline.
Novo’s chief rival Eli Lilly stole headlines at the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) annual meeting a few weeks ago, revealing robust weight loss generated by a combination of its amylin agonist eloralintide and powerhouse dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist Zepbound. In the Phase 2b trial, patients with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes who took the combo, called EloraTZP, lost an average of 23.3% of their weight at the 48-week mark, compared to 14.8% for those given Zepbound alone and 3% for placebo comparators.
Obesity
Superior weight loss, blood sugar control propel Lilly’s amylin-GIP/GLP-1 combo into Phase 3
EloraTZP—a combination of an amylin asset and Eli Lilly’s approved obesity drug Zepbound—made a clean sweep of the primary and secondary endpoints in a mid-stage trial of adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, setting up the launch of a Phase 3 trial before the end of the year.

The trial did record muddled safety data, with adverse event–tied discontinuations across the dosing groups of EloraTZP ranging from 10.8% and 27%, compared with 0% to 10.8% for eloralintide alone, 2.9% for tirzepatide only and 16.7% for placebo.
EloraTZP’s Phase 2 results were “met with mixed reaction owing to the tolerability trade-off,” BNP Paribas wrote in an Oct. 5 note, which noted tolerability as a key theme at EASD.
Nevertheless, the data package as a whole was enough for Lilly to take EloraTZP to Phase 3. Meanwhile, the pharma is expecting results from a Phase 3 study of eloralintide as a monotherapy in 2028. Analysts are expecting big things from the drug.
“We expect eloralintide to be a mega-blockbuster given its differentiated benefit-tolerability profile and potential role for patients who failed GLP-1 therapy due to efficacy or tolerability challenges,” Leerink Partners wrote in a note to investors on Sept. 15.
As for Zealand’s Roche-partnered petrelintide, the companies reported Phase 2 data last week that William Blair found both “intriguing” and “underwhelming.” The long-acting human amylin analog elicited up to 9.2% mean weight loss at week 28 depending on the dose—which William Blair said was comparable to eloralintide and Zepbound and superior to Wegovy at the same time point. But the analysts were less impressed by petrelintide’s ability to lower blood sugar.
This isn’t the first time petrelintide has failed to impress analysts and investors. In March, the investigational drug lowered body weight by more than 10% after 42 weeks in a mid-stage study . While the result fell well short of analyst expectations, minimal side effects were reported in the trial.
“We believe Zealand achieved the goal of demonstrating highly encouraging tolerability for petrelintide, though the magnitude of weight loss disappointed,” William Blair wrote at the time.
As clinical data begin to differentiate the field, Novo is looking ahead to a potential launch of CagriSema. The asset has had a rocky developmental journey, missing Novo’s own projections for the therapy in a December 2024 readout from the Phase 3 REDEFINE 1 trial and falling to Zepbound in the head-to-head Phase 3 REDEFINE 4 trial in February. Last month, however, CagriSema did best Lilly’s GIP/GLP-1 agonist in another Phase 3 test, REIMAGINE 5 .
Seigerman described CagriSema as “a bit of a sleeper asset.”
Whichever next-gen weight loss assets eventually steal market share, amylin will almost undoubtedly be among them. Seigerman cited his conversation about how it may have been the top choice over GLP-1s if the field could start over.
“That says to me,” he said, “that amylin is going to be very important.”

1970 Mustang Emerges From a Junkyard, Owner Has Bad News: Parked Outside for an Extended Period
27 photos
Photo: eBay seller semcom
This first-generation Mustang has been sitting outdoors for an extended period. This is all you need to know about this 1970 Ford project, as the owner has decided to let the car go and see if anyone out there is willing to give it a second chance.
Just like any other car sitting in a junkyard, it struggles with lots of issues, but considering how many parts still look to be available, I wouldn’t be surprised to see this Mustang finding a home fast. It all comes down to the price and what you’ll find when you check it out in person.
A car in this shape doesn’t typically qualify as a restoration candidate but rather as a donor, but my recommendation is to call the seller and ask for a digital walkaround video. This should help you figure out how many repairs it needs because turning it into a project - a father-son project, if you wish - could still be possible. Many cars in worse shape have already been restored, so maybe this Mustang can get this long-overdue treatment, too.
Photo: eBay seller semcom The 1970 Mustang didn’t get significant updates, pretty much because the changes the car received in 1969 were so significant that further notable refinements weren’t necessary.
Ford ended the year with over 190,000 Mustangs rolling off the assembly lines, and the hardtop once again accounted for the lion’s share with 82,569 units. The fastback continued to be particularly popular, receiving 45,934 orders, with the Mach 1 claiming third place.
This was the second year for the Mach 1, and after making the GT redundant in 1969, it returned to account for over 40,900 orders.
The hardtop remained the most affordable version, which kind of explains why most people picked this body style. It started at $2,721, while the Mach 1 was significantly more expensive at $3,271. The base convertible was available from $3,025.
Photo: eBay seller semcom The Mustang continued to be offered with a wide range of engines, pretty much because Ford wanted the car to tackle a range of customers as varied as possible. As a result, people who were considering a Mustang for a daily driver could get a 250 six rated at 155 horsepower, while buyers who wanted a small rocket on wheels could go as high as a 429 developing 375 horsepower.
Unsurprisingly, this massive engine upgrade came with a huge price increase, as the 429 could be installed on the Mustang for $1,208 more.
This engine allowed Ford to maintain its NASCAR appetite, and according to various sources, only 499 Mustangs fitted with this configuration ended up seeing the daylight.
Photo: eBay seller semcom This particular Mustang has obviously seen better days, and the engine that was once under the hood is no longer relevant unless you want to restore it to day-one specifications. That wouldn’t make much sense, considering its shape, so throwing whatever engine you have around in there should be the most convenient solution.
The car suffers from obvious rust problems, and this isn’t a surprise. A pile of metal sitting outside for an extended period ends up struggling with severe corrosion, so you’d better call your metal guy and get him ready for quite a lot of work. New panels will obviously be required, but that’s why I recommended that you request a walkaround video before anything else.
The cabin doesn’t look better, but there are several big parts in there. The seller advertises “original components,” but I don’t think this Mustang can be considered a candidate for an all-original restoration project.
Photo: eBay seller semcom One of the most intriguing tidbits on this Mustang is the odometer. If you get inside and check the odo, the number you’ll see on the clock is impressive. The odometer reads 21,909 miles, but it’s unclear if this is the actual mileage. I would specifically look into this because a low-mile Mustang, even abandoned in a junkyard, isn’t something you see every day.
As with every car suffering from such major issues, it all comes down to the selling price. It goes without saying that a Mustang in this condition can’t sell for high dollars, and the seller looks to be well aware of this.
They listed the car for auction, and what’s more, no reserve has been configured. This means you can get the car for only $1,899 if no one else joins the digital battle for this Mustang. If you want to get your hands on it without a fight, you can trigger the Buy It Now option and pay $2,495 to buy the Mustang.
The vehicle is parked in Commerce, Georgia, and you will also need transportation (so make sure you consider the additional costs), given the only thing you’ll find under the hood is a lot of fresh air. The car sells with a bill of sale, and no other papers are available.

Jeep Reveals Everything New About The 2027 Cherokee: Trailhawk, Shades, Trims, Pricing, and More
7 photos
Photo: Jeep
The specialty US automaker Jeep wants to talk about the 2027 Cherokee at large, after it previously focused on the most important grade for the new model year: Trailhawk.
Back at the end of September 2026, we found out that the fully redesigned Cherokee has also been turned into a proper crossover SUV with off-road chops for model year 2027, with prices kicking off at $44,625 in the United States’ automotive market for the 2027 Cherokee Trailhawk Hybrid, which comes with goodies like a raised suspension, rear locker, low range, and a 37.5:1 crawl ratio, among others.
We quickly covered the novelties and then focused on how does the all-new off-road machine compare to its direct rivals. The sixth-generation KM compact crossover SUV has been morphed into a proper off-road adventurer, and we needed to know if it can also handle its competition, not just the trails. And there’s a bunch of them, like the 2026 Ford Bronco Sport Badlands, the 2027 Honda CR-V TrailSport Hybrid, the all-new 2026 Toyota RAV4 Woodland, or the 2026 Forester Wilderness, just to name a few.
But now it’s time to know everything that’s new for the 2027 Jeep Cherokee family: introduced as an all-new generation for the 2026 model year, the sixth by its name, the latest Cherokee “expands customer choice with new trims, features and the highly anticipated Trailhawk model .” All versions of the 2027 Jeep Cherokee feature a 1.6-liter inline-four Turbo Hybrid powertrain that has 210 hp combined, up to an estimated 37 mpg combined, including 39 mpg city, and 500-plus miles on a single tank of fuel.
“It is the most fuel-efficient Jeep model ever, without a plug,” says its parent Stellantis, and the towing capacity is 3,500 pounds while the SUV also boasts best-in-class off-road prowess in terms of approach, breakover, and departure angles. Also, when properly equipped, it is said to be the “only vehicle in its class to offer a 24-inch water fording rating depth.”
Anyway, the Trail Rated Jeep Cherokee Trailhawk returns for the 2027 model year with the two-speed power transfer unit with Active Drive II 4x4, Rock Mode has a 2.92 low range ratio and 37.5:1 crawl ratio, bespoke front and rear fascias, red tow hooks, skid plates, an off-road suspension, and 17-inch alloy wheels with all-terrain tires.
The other trim levels are Cherokee, Laredo and Laredo Altitude, Limited and Limited Altitude, Trailhawk, plus Overland, with pricing kicking off at $37,125, including a $1,995 destination charge, for the base model, and $44,625 for the Cherokee Trailhawk, including a $1,995 destination charge. The Jeep Cherokee Limited Altitude and Laredo Altitude are also new, packing 18-inch gloss black aluminum wheels, gloss black exterior accents and badges, and a gloss painted roof (Limited Altitude) or a Capri leatherette seat fabric with suede inserts on Laredo Altitude.
The available colors also include novelties: Fathom Blue, Ghost, Copper Shino, and Goldilocks join the fray alongside Bright White, Diamond Black, Sting Gray, Red Hot, Hydro Blue, and ’41. Inside, the hues are Global Black or Arctic, as well as the new Mantis Green, which is exclusive to the Trailhawk. Ordering is now open, including for the all-new and returning 2027 Jeep Cherokee Trailhawk, and manufacturing takes place at the Toluca Assembly Plant in Toluca, Mexico .
So, what do you think of the 2027 Cherokee - yay or nay?

One-of-One 1968 Mustang GT Fastback 428 Cobra Jet With 4.30 Gears Forced To Leave Private Collection
31 photos
Photo: GTS Classic Motors
"What's the greatest engine Ford Motor Company ever made?" The answer to that will take up some very heated debate, and a lot of internet - and it still wouldn't set things straight. But the Cobra Jet is definitely among the finalists. Born at the height of the classic Detroit horsepower wars, this 428-cubic-inch V8 transformed the humble pony car into an undisputed quarter-mile terror during the 1968 season.
Before the R-code powerhouse arrived, Mustang buyers craving big-block displacement had to settle for the S-code 390-cubic-inch V8, which struggled to hold off rival Chrysler and General Motors machines. Rhode Island dealer Bob Tasca pioneered the winning formula by mating a 428-cubic-inch Police Interceptor block with free-breathing 427-cubic-inch Low-Riser cylinder heads, heavy-duty exhaust manifolds, a cast-iron intake, and a 735-cfm Holley four-barrel carburetor fed through a functional Ram Air hood scoop.
Ford proved the concept in February 1968 at the Pomona NHRA Winternationals with 50 Wimbledon White lightweight fastbacks before launching showroom sales on April 1, 1968. That mid-year release swept the Shelby Mustang off its wheels by offering superior straight-line performance in a regular Mustang at a lower cost. Ultimately, it built the wall and put the writing on it declaring the dusk of the fabled Carroll Shelby muscle pony program.
Although the 1968 Shelby GT500KR shared the exact same 428-cubic-inch Cobra Jet engine, the heavily stylized Shelby carried extra weight and a hefty $4,473 sticker price. Street racers quickly realized a regular Ford Mustang fastback packed identical mechanical punch in a lighter, subtler body without the luxury markup. One of the finest surviving examples of that mid-year breed is now offered by collector Ben Shearman.
Photo: GTS Classic Motors Showcased in a walkaround video on the GTS Classic Motors YouTube channel, this 1968½ Ford Mustang GT Fastback 428 Cobra Jet comes directly from the personal collection of Ben Shearman. Finished in factory Wimbledon White, the numbers-matching R-code fastback pairs its 428-cubic-inch V8 with a factory 4-speed manual transmission and the ultra-rare factory 4.30 Traction-Lok rear axle, a combination that makes it a 1-of-1 build per its Deluxe Marti Report.
Whoever ordered this Mustang in 1968 had only drag-strip dominance in mind, specifying a blue standard interior, radio delete, manual steering, no fold-down rear seat, and virtually no extra weight-adding options. Its provenance is backed by the Deluxe Marti Report, owner's manual, period dealer literature, and Cobra Jet 50th Anniversary memorabilia. The package even includes a photograph hand-signed by legendary 1968 Cobra Jet drag racer Al Joniec holding a winner's trophy.
Fresh off a three-year concours rotisserie restoration, the laser-straight body wears high-gloss Wimbledon White paint that pays homage to the original 50 lightweight race cars. It retains the signature black 1968.5 Cobra Jet hood stripe and a dark blue GT side stripe, riding on GT wheels with trim rings and brand-new Goodyear Polyglas tires. Underneath, the chassis replicates Dearborn assembly-line perfection with proper primers, factory overspray patterns, and inspection stamps.
Photo: GTS Classic Motors Under the hood, the correct 428-cubic-inch Cobra Jet V8 displays every period-authentic component, including the rare starter delay system, proper S-tube, smog equipment, correct carburetor, fuel pump, hanging radiator tag, battery, and 1968-only trim. With 25 sorting miles logged since completion, the big-block starts effortlessly and idles like it knows people in high places. Inside, the restored blue cabin presents as new, down to the Autolite floor mat and Dearborn final acceptance markings.
Production figures highlight just how scarce this mid-year brute truly is. Out of 317,423 Mustangs built for the 1968 model year, only 17,458 cars received the GT Equipment Group across the board. That includes 289s, 302s, S-code 390s (any Bullitt fans out there?), and the mighty 428 V8 options.
Counting both Ford and Shelby assembly lines, total 1968 production with the R-code 428-cubic-inch Cobra Jet engine reached 2,870 vehicles, split between 1,571 Shelby GT500KR models and 1,299 regular non-Shelby Ford Mustangs.
Photo: GTS Classic Motors Every retail 1968 R-code Mustang came with the mandatory GT package, dividing those 1,299 cars into 1,044 fastbacks, 221 hardtop coupes, and 34 convertibles. Buyers could pair the formidable big-block V8 only with a heavy-duty Toploader 4-speed manual or a C6 3-speed automatic, with 792 of the 1,044 fastbacks receiving the 4-speed and 252 getting the automatic. When new, a $2,712 fastback with the $421 engine and $147 GT package cost $3,280.
On paper, Ford rated the 7.0-liter Cobra Jet V8 with its 10.6:1 compression ratio at a conservative 335 horsepower at 5,200 rpm and 440 lb-ft of torque at 3,400 rpm, though real output approached 410 horsepower. Period magazine testers in 1968 clocked 0 to 60 mph in 5.4 seconds, the eighth-mile in 9.54 seconds at 82.5 mph, the quarter-mile in 13.56 seconds at 106 mph, and a 129-mph top speed.
As the owner and seller notes during his walkaround, the beauty of a 1968.5 Cobra Jet GT fastback lay in its understated street presence, often fooling unsuspecting rivals into thinking they were lining up against a mild 390-cubic-inch Mustang. Once the four-speed and 4.30 gears hooked up, competitors only saw taillights. No joke – Hemi Mopars found out the hard way at the Pomona Winternationals, when the Cobra Jets eliminated everyone lining up against the white Mustangs.

At the European Society of Medical Oncology meeting in Madrid this weekend, analysts will be watching for detailed data on Merck and Moderna’s personalized cancer vaccine, Summit and Akeso’s PD-1xVEGF bispecific therapy, and a host of antibody-drug conjugates.
Antibody-drug conjugates, a groundbreaking cancer vaccine under development by Merck and Moderna and a closely watched PD-1xVEGF bispecific therapy from Summit Therapeutics and Akeso will be top of mind when the world’s foremost oncology experts convene in Madrid for this year’s meeting of the European Society of Medical Oncology.
True to its reputation, the 2026 edition of ESMO will feature some of most impactful research across biopharma, providing a stage for studies that could potentially alter how cancer is managed and treated.
“It will be a big year,” Dara Azar, associate vice president of Biotech Equity Research at Stifel, told BioSpace in an email. “We have a win in cancer vaccines and the immediate next question is, what is next? Where can investors find the next opportunity?”
Here, BioSpace previews some of the most highly anticipated presentations of the meeting, which kicks off on Friday.
Merck, Moderna seize the spotlight
Arguably the most highly anticipated presentation at ESMO belongs to Merck and Moderna. In August, the partners revealed that their mRNA-based personalized cancer vaccine intismeran autogene, when combined with the anti-PD-1 powerhouse Keytruda, extended survival without disease recurrence for patients with melanoma in the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial . The trial comprised 1,137 patients randomized 2:1 to receive up to nine doses of the vaccine every three weeks and Keytruda for up to one year or single-agent Keytruda for approximately one year after surgical removal of cutaneous melanoma.
Cancer
Moderna stock nearly doubles as Merck-partnered mRNA cancer vaccine meets Phase 3 goal
Melanoma was slower to recur in patients receiving Merck and Moderna’s mRNA vaccine with Keytruda, supporting use of the combination in adjuvant treatment. The partners plan to take the data to the FDA.
August 19, 2026
·
3 min read
·
Nick Paul Taylor
Read more
On Saturday, Merck and Moderna are scheduled to present more detailed findings from this study.
“Positive Phase 3 melanoma data could move personalized cancer vaccines from a decades-old scientific ambition toward a treatment physicians may actually use at scale,” Mitchell Kapoor, senior analyst at H.C. Wainwright, told BioSpace in an email.
For Merck and Moderna, the bar is high. A previous, mid-stage readout in June found that after more than 60 months, intismeran autogene plus Keytruda cut the risk of death or recurrence by 49% versus the PD-1 blocker alone. These findings come from the Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 trial , which enrolled 157 patients with melanoma who had undergone complete resection and who are at a high risk of recurrence. Recurrence-free survival (RFS) was the primary endpoint.
The investigational regimen also slashed the risk of metastasis or death by 59% and improved overall survival by 53%, as per the June data drop. “The Phase 2 benchmark creates lofty expectations,” Kapoor said. “The real test here is how much of that extraordinary Phase 2 effect survives when the patient numbers scale from 157 patients to more than 1,100.”
After the topline INTerpath-001 disclosure, investors want to see the qualitative magnitude of efficacy “to better understand [the vaccine’s] competitiveness in not only adjuvant melanoma, but also other cancer types,” Jefferies Managing Director Andrew Tsai told BioSpace over email.
Stifel’s Azar agreed. “It’s important to remember that melanoma is believed to be ‘a lower hanging fruit’ for personalized cancer vaccines. ” INTerpath-001 is a good first step for intismeran autogene, Azar said, but “the big question is: can cancer vaccines access the more complex indications with just the doublet or do they need more immune activation?”
The analysts could soon have at least one more dataset to reference. Tsai told BioSpace last month that he is expecting a readout for a Phase 2 trial of intismeran autogene in renal cell carcinoma later this year or in early 2027.
Meanwhile, in melanoma, investors are expecting an RFS benefit of at least 30%, Tsai said, adding that “in theory, a stronger benefit should translate to stronger commercial adoption.” A more pronounced therapeutic effect could also have “stronger readacross to other cancer types.”
Merck and Moderna are also testing the intismeran autogene/Keytruda combo in a host of other cancer types, including non-small cell lung cancer and bladder cancer.
In melanoma alone, Jefferies expects intismeran autogene’s peak unadjusted sales to top $3 billion. Unlocking other indications would broaden the vaccine’s patient pool and increase its peak sales potential “considerably,” Tsai said.
A ‘big year’ for ADCs
Aside from a detailed description of its Moderna-partnered vaccine victory, Merck is scheduled to unveil data from a Phase 3 trial of another closely watched asset: the Kelun-Biotech–partnered ADC sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT), being tested in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
“ADCs could change first-line cancer treatment while helping Merck defend its $30B-plus Keytruda franchise,” Wainwright’s Kapoor said. The Phase 3 OptiTROP-Lung06 trial combines sac-TMT with Keytruda as a first-line treatment for patients with PD-L1-negative non-squamous NSCLC.
Findings toplined in July showed that sac-TMT plus Keytruda and chemotherapy met the study’s primary endpoint, meaningfully improving progression-free survival as compared to Keytruda plus chemotherapy. There was also a positive trend in overall survival, a key secondary endpoint.
Lung cancer
Kelun’s Merck-partnered ADC notches late-stage NSCLC win alongside Keytruda
The Phase 3 results are the first direct proof-of-concept for an ADC replacing platinum-based chemo in a first-line standard-of-care regimen for non-small cell lung cancer, according to Leerink Partners. The readout also represents the second late-stage win for the Merck and Kelun-Biotech asset, called sac-TMT.
July 15, 2026
·
2 min read
·
Michael Gibney
Read more
The partners did not provide specific data at the time; they will during a Sunday presentation at ESMO, which could provide a better view of sac-TMT’s benefit-risk profile in this setting.
“A large improvement with manageable side effects could keep doctors prescribing Keytruda and generate new ADC revenue as Keytruda’s primary U.S. patent expires in 2028,” Kapoor said. Keytruda brought in $31.7 billion last year , hanging on to its crown as the single top-selling pharma product.
Stifel’s Azar similarly pointed to OptiTROP-Lung06 as a potentially impactful presentation at ESMO, noting that the trial is “a great case study” for a combinable ADC challenging platinum-based chemo in a frontline lung cancer setting.
Another ADC that analysts expect to make waves at ESMO is AstraZeneca’s sonesitatug vedotin (sone-ve), which the pharma gained access to in its February 2023 licensing deal with China’s KYM Biosciences for $63 million upfront. The asset targets Claudin-18.2, a protein commonly expressed in the stomach lining.
AstraZeneca is evaluating sone-ve in the Phase 3 CLARITY-Gastric01 trial in second-line or later disease versus an investigator’s choice of comparator therapy. The study includes patients with advanced or metastatic gastric cancer, gastroesophageal junction cancer or distal esophageal adenocarcinoma with CLDN18.2 expression in at least 25% of tumor cells.
Early findings released in July showed that sone-ve aced the trial’s overall survival endpoint but only demonstrated “a trend toward improved PFS,” the other co-primary endpoint, AstraZeneca said at the time . The pharma has big plans for sone-ve and last month inked an agreement with Summit to test combinations of the ADC with the biotech’s PD-1xVEGF bispecific therapy ivonescimab, primarily focusing on gastrointestinal cancers.
As in the case of sac-TMT, analysts are closely watching for detailed data from CLARITY-Gastric01, with an eye toward getting a clear view of sone-ve’s benefit-risk balance.
“The biggest ADC opportunities could belong to drugs that replace conventional chemo, work after another ADC fails, or make effective ADC treatment easier to continue at an adequate dose intensity,” Kapoor said.
It is shaping up to be “a big year for ADCs,” Azar agreed.
Not just a Big Pharma game
While Big Pharma has typically dominated the major conferences, this year’s ESMO will also feature some of biopharma’s most promising emergent drugmakers.
Leading this list is Summit with ivonescimab. The Akeso-partnered therapy first made waves in September 2024 when it significantly outperformed Keytruda in a Phase 3 NSCLC study in China.
At ESMO on Sunday, Summit and China-based Akeso are presenting data for the candidate in a different type of malignancy: gastrointestinal cancers. In the Phase 3 HARMONi-GI1 study , the companies are combining the investigational bispecific with chemotherapy for the first-line treatment of patients with advanced biliary tract cancer—and pitting the regimen against AstraZeneca’s Imfinzi plus chemotherapy.
Topline results in August showed that the ivonescimab combo significantly improved overall survival versus the Imfinzi control, meeting the study’s primary endpoint. The trial also revealed significant benefits in progression-free survival and objective response rate, key secondary endpoints. The partners did not provide specific data at the time but are expected to at ESMO.
“It’s interesting that [ivonescimab] continues to deliver positive Phase 3 results from China, also outside of lung cancer and against different immunotherapy comparators,” Stifel’s Azar told BioSpace .
Ivonescimab is under FDA review for advanced non-squamous NSCLC, with a decision expected by Nov. 14 . Summit has not specified a timeline for FDA submission in other solid tumor indications.
Also arriving in Madrid is Incyte Corporation, bringing what Wainwright’s Kapoor calls “one of the most important catalysts at ESMO as pancreatic cancer has become a multibillion-dollar opportunity for RAS-targeted drugs.”
The biotech is scheduled to present data from the Phase 3 DAWN-303 study of INCB161734 , an investigational oral inhibitor that selectively targets the G12D-mutated versions of the KRAS protein.
In this arena, Incyte is facing off against Revolution Medicines, which is advancing zoldonrasib, an asset with a similar targeting profile. The selective G12D inhibitor achieved an 82% overall response rate when used with the chemotherapy backbone mFOLFIRINOX, as per a Phase 1/2 readout in June.
Revolution made waves in April when its RAS(ON) multi-selective, non-covalent inhibitor daraxonrasib doubled overall survival in a Phase 3 study in pancreatic cancer. The drug was greenlit in August with the brand name Rasonque, but FDA review documents released following the approval showed that the drug performed less well in participants with G12D mutations, leading to an overall response rate (ORR) of 24%, as compared with the 33% ORR seen across the study and the 50% ORR seen in patients with a G12V mutation.
For Incyte, keeping disease under control in around four out of five patients would be “compelling” given manageable toxicity, said Kapoor, who is looking forward to INCB161734’s readout at ESMO. At that threshold, he continued, “the focus becomes how much of the first-line opportunity Incyte can grab.”

High-quality cytokines for organoid growth, differentiation, and expansion
Introduction Organoids are three-dimensional, self-organizing models derived from stem cells that recapitulate key structural and functional features of in vivo tissues. Cytokines and growth factors provide essential niche signals that regulate stem cell proliferation, self-renewal, and differentiation¹ , ². Classical factors such as R-spondin 1 (RSPO1) , EGF , Noggin and Wnt3a, together with tissue-specific and emerging signals such as FGFs , NRG1 , and IGF2 , support organoid establishment, expansion, and differentiation³ , ⁴. With growing applications in disease modeling, drug screening, and precision medicine, reliable cytokines are increasingly important for reproducible organoid culture⁴. Sino Biological provides high-quality cytokines with validated bioactivity and consistent performance to support diverse organoid culture and research applications.
Cytokine Signaling in Organoid Culture Organoid culture depends on the reconstruction of signaling environments that normally govern cell fate within tissues. Rather than acting independently, cytokines and growth factors form interconnected signaling networks that balance stem cell maintenance, proliferation, and differentiation. A classic example is the WENR system, in which Wnt3a and RSPO1 reinforce Wnt/β-catenin signaling, EGF promotes epithelial proliferation, and Noggin suppresses BMP signaling to help maintain the stem/progenitor state⁵ , ⁶. Beyond this core framework, tissue- and stage-specific signals further shape lineage commitment, maturation, and cellular composition. Recent organoid systems increasingly incorporate additional FGF, TGF-β/BMP, Notch, and other pathways to reproduce more complex tissue patterning and cellular interactions⁷. The composition and timing of these signals can therefore profoundly influence organoid identity and phenotype, enabling the development of models that more closely reflect the biology of their tissues of origin.
Figure 1. Key signaling pathways and representative cytokines and growth factors involved in organoid development. Tissue-specific combinations of cytokines and growth factors regulate major signaling pathways, including FGF, WNT, BMP, and NOTCH signaling, to guide lineage commitment and the development of brain, retinal, lung, cardiac, liver, kidney, and vascular organoids. Representative factors commonly used in these culture systems are shown.
From Cytokine-Guided Culture to Translational Applications The ability to precisely control cytokine and growth factor signaling has expanded organoids from experimental 3D cultures into increasingly relevant models for translational research. Defined culture conditions support the establishment and expansion of tissue- and patient-derived organoids while helping preserve key cellular, molecular, and functional features of their tissues of origin⁸ , ⁹. These models provide biologically relevant platforms for disease modeling, drug efficacy and toxicity testing, and preclinical therapeutic development⁸. Patient-derived organoids further capture inter-patient heterogeneity and can be used to evaluate individualized treatment responses, supporting their growing potential in precision medicine⁹ , ¹⁰. Importantly, reproducible cytokine and growth factor conditions are essential for generating consistent organoid phenotypes and reliable downstream readouts¹¹. Table 1. Translational Applications of Cytokine-Guided Organoid Models
Application | What Organoids Offer | Role of Cytokines & Growth Factors
Disease Modeling | Mimic tissue structure and function Reproduce key disease features | Maintain tissue-specific cell types Support disease-related phenotypes
Drug Screening | Test drug efficacy Evaluate drug toxicity | Support stable organoid growth Improve experimental consistency
Cancer Research | Model patient tumors Preserve tumor heterogeneity | Support tumor organoid growth Maintain tumor cell diversity
Precision Medicine | Compare treatment options Predict individual drug responses | Maintain patient-derived organoids Support reliable drug testing
Regenerative Medicine | Expand tissue-specific cells Support tissue repair research | Promote cell expansion Guide differentiation and maturation
Developmental Research | Model tissue formation and development Study changes in cell fate | Recreate developmental signals Guide tissue-specific differentiation
Applications in Research Recombinant growth factors are widely used to establish and maintain organoid models across different tissue types. For example, EGF and bFGF have been incorporated into culture systems for the generation of mouse pancreatic ductal organoids (Figure 2), providing an ex vivo model for studying pancreatic epithelial biology. Similarly, R-Spondin has been used as a key component of mouse colonic organoid culture, supporting the transition from isolated colonic crypts to established organoids (Figure 2). These examples illustrate how defined growth factors can support organoid-based studies across diverse tissue models.
Figure 2. Application of recombinant growth factors in pancreatic ductal organoid culture. Representative bright-field images of mouse pancreatic ductal organoids cultured under Org and 4F conditions. Recombinant murine EGF and human bFGF from Sino Biological were included in the 4F culture medium to support pancreatic ductal organoid generation. Source: doi: 10.3724/abbs.2024218
Figure 3. Application of R-Spondin in mouse colonic organoid culture. Representative images showing(A) freshly isolated mouse colonic crypts and (B) colonic organoids after 5 days of culture R-Spondin (cat# 11083-HNAS ) was included as a component of the organoid culture medium. Source: doi: 10.1093/carcin/bgt412
Sino Biological Solutions for Organoid Research Sino Biological provides a comprehensive portfolio of cytokines and growth factors to support organoid establishment, expansion, differentiation, and functional research across diverse organoid models. Its organoid research solutions cover 3D organoid culture, physiological organoids, and tumor organoids, providing researchers with relevant signaling factors for different tissue types, culture stages, and research applications.
Table 2. Featured cytokines in organoid culture
Featured Cytokine / Growth Factor | Cat. No. | Key Features

Noggin / NOG | 50688-M02H | >85% SDS-PAGE · hFc Tag · Active
R-Spondin 1 / RSPO1 | 11083-HNAS | ≥95% SEC-HPLC · Native · Active
FGF2 / bFGF | 10014-HNAE | ≥95% SDS-PAGE · Native · Active
FGF10 | 10573-HNAE | ≥95% SEC-HPLC · Native · Active
Activin A | 10429-HNAH | ≥95% SEC-HPLC · Native · Active
IL-22 | 13059-HNAE | >95% SDS-PAGE · Native · Active
VEGF165 | 11066-HNAH | ≥95% SEC-HPLC · Native · Active
TGF-β1 | 10804-HNAC | >95% SDS-PAGE · Native · Active
IL-13 | 10369-HNAC | ≥95% SEC-HPLC · Native · Active
FGF4 | 16043-HNAE | ≥95% SEC-HPLC · Native · Active
